problem:
The equation below describes all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(3,0,-2)$ and $Q(1,1,-1).$

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ b \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t\in [c,1]
$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Line

feedback.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $F(-5,-2,4)$ and $G(3,-1,1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $F$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=f+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $f$ is the position vector of $F.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $F(-5,-2,4)$ and $G(3,-1,1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{FG} \\  & =⟨3,-1,1⟩-⟨-5,-2,4⟩ \\  & =⟨8,1,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
